clue.text: Large knife and tear gas confines the unruly

indicators.note: to confine is to hold something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Mace is a brand of tear gas spray

indicators.note: unruly letters are out of order and get rearranged

explanation.surface: A riot scene: weapons and tear gas used to hold back a disorderly crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the unruly' reads as a disorderly mob, but 'unruly' only shuffles the word 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: A long broad-bladed chopping knife used for cutting vegetation is a classic big blade.

clue.text: Division brought about by Spooner's wee pal

indicators.note: Spooner's means the first sounds of the two words are swapped

parts.note: to wee is to widdle, a childish word for urinating
a pal is a mate

explanation.surface: A friend's toilet trip causing a falling-out.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the first sounds of WIDDLE MATE gives MIDDLE WAIT, said like the boxing class.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxing is split into weight classes, and this is one of those divisions.

clue.text: Fantastic ski chalet as white and dusty as can be

definitions.text: white and dusty as can be

indicators.note: fantastic means fanciful, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wonderful snowy ski lodge, white and powdery.
explanation.definitionFit: Chalk is white and powdery, so the superlative means most like chalk.

clue.text: Husband, perhaps, scratching bottom then looking up to seduce

indicators.note: in a down clue, looking up means the letters read upwards, backwards
scratching means removing, and bottom is the last letter

parts.note: a husband is an example of a partner

explanation.surface: A husband scratching his backside then glancing up to woo someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scratching bottom' drops R to leave PARTNE; 'looking up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: To lure someone into a trap or temptation is to ensnare them.

clue.text: Goes to ground in suit, head lowered

indicators.note: head lowered means the first letter moves down the word

parts.note: hearts is one of the four card suits

explanation.surface: Someone hiding in a suit, head bowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head lowered' moves the H of HEARTS from top to bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A fox earths when it takes refuge in its burrow, going to ground.

clue.text: Thoroughfare ready for bar

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a thoroughfare
fruit that is ready to eat is ripe

explanation.surface: A busy street primed for a new pub or drinking spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A band or line of colour, as on a flag or a uniform, is a bar of that colour.

clue.text: Get rid of solicitor for fight to the death?

parts.note: to shoo is to chase away
a tout is someone who solicits custom

explanation.surface: Firing a lawyer in favour of a duel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solicitor' suggests a lawyer, but here it is one who solicits trade.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun battle ending with one side dead is a deadly fight; the question mark marks the loose fit.

clue.text: Charity is embarrassed and angry

parts.note: embarrassed people go red
angry means cross

explanation.surface: An awkward, furious charity.
explanation.definitionFit: The international humanitarian organisation is a well-known charity.

clue.text: A working president, once

parts.note: a, as in 'once a week', means per
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: A former leader who held a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Juan Perón was president of Argentina, a former head of state.

clue.text: Produce wind audibly

indicators.note: audibly means the word for wind is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a draught is a current of air, a light wind

explanation.surface: An instruction to break wind noisily.
explanation.definitionFit: To write a first version of a document is to compose or create it.

clue.text: Judicial officers not beginning to cook books again

indicators.note: not means the following letter is left out of the officers' title

parts.note: in England a recorder is a barrister sitting as a part-time judge

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Court officials refusing to begin falsifying the accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cook the books' suggests fraud, but 'books again' is the definition: arranges another booking.
explanation.definitionFit: To book something again, such as a delivery or stock, is to place another order for it.

clue.text: Evaluations of certain fellows protected by dodgy mates

indicators.note: protected by means held inside the other letters
dodgy means suspect or unsound, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: certain means sure
fellows are men

explanation.surface: Assessing some men sheltered by shady friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dodgy' turns MATES into MEATS, which surrounds SURE MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Measuring something gives a figure that assesses or appraises it.

clue.text: Fancy a drink? Unhesitatingly

parts.note: to fancy something is to like it
a shot is a small measure of spirits

explanation.surface: An offer of a drink, and the eager reply.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means immediately and eagerly, as fast as a bullet leaves a gun.

clue.text: Extent of ire when cycling

indicators.note: cycling means the last letter is moved round to the front of the word for ire

parts.note: ire is anger

explanation.surface: How far a cyclist's road rage reaches.
explanation.definitionFit: The scope or reach of something is its span, as in the range of a gun.

clue.text: Wife and wife-to-be meet at what time?

parts.note: a bride-to-be is the hen at a hen party, the British bachelorette night

explanation.surface: A wife and a fiancée are meeting; the question is the time.
explanation.definitionFit: The question word asks for a time, exactly as the phrase does.

clue.text: Commuter halts breast enlargements, perhaps, in which piece of silicone is implanted

indicators.note: in which, with is implanted, says one letter goes into the operations
implanted means set inside, so the letter goes into the other piece

parts.note: breast enlargements are examples of bust ops, operations on the bust

indicators.note: a piece of a word here is its first letter

explanation.surface: Cosmetic surgery stopped, with a bit of silicone implant mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in which ... is implanted' puts the S from silicone inside BUST OPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Places where commuters' buses pull up and pause are halts on a route.

clue.text: What makes a female regularly covet Seth, the actor and comedian

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the words

parts.note: Seth Rogen is a Canadian actor and comedian

explanation.surface: Envying Seth, the comic actor, as the thing that makes a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Seth does double duty: his name gives letters to the alternate pick and also identifies the comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: This primary sex hormone produces female characteristics.

clue.text: Standing of President Trump is getting eroded, principally

indicators.note: principally means taking the leading letter of each word

explanation.surface: A president's reputation being worn away.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing as status or reputation is a synonym for high regard.

clue.text: Coy son injured in fight with young badger?

indicators.note: in means the rearranged letters go inside the fight

parts.note: a bout is a boxing fight

indicators.note: injured means damaged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shy boy hurt in a fight with a young animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injured' makes OYSC from COY + S. 'badger' is not the animal: a scout collects badges.
explanation.definitionFit: A youngster in the Scouts earns badges, so is jokingly one who badges.

clue.text: Bury gold around island's centre

indicators.note: around means the letters go round the island letter

parts.note: to inter is to bury
OR is gold in heraldry
I is the abbreviation for island; the 's links it to the definition

explanation.surface: Burying treasure in the middle of an island.
explanation.definitionFit: The inside or inner part of something is its middle, as the interior of a country.

clue.text: Royalists are imprisoning emperor

indicators.note: imprisoning means the words hold the answer locked inside them

explanation.surface: Monarchists have locked up a ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian ruler's title was a form of Caesar, meaning an emperor.

clue.text: Dog breed's first desirable characteristic

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: an asset is a valuable quality

explanation.surface: The top trait of a dog breed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog breed' wants to be the definition, but 'breed's first' gives the B.
explanation.definitionFit: This short-legged long-eared hound is a breed of dog.

clue.text: Autocrat is very downcast when northern den is obliterated

indicators.note: obliterated means wiped out, so these letters are removed

parts.note: despondent means deeply dejected
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tyrant is gloomy after his northern hideout is destroyed.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruler with absolute power, often a tyrant, is an autocrat.

clue.text: Tolerates journalists

definitions.meaning: to hack it is to cope with or put up with something

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the verb for bearing something and the slang for reporters.

clue.text: One involved in fraudulent schemes fabricates money

indicators.note: involved in means placed inside

parts.note: cons are swindles
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A swindler forging cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A mint stamps metal into currency, making money, as the verb describes.

clue.text: The recipient of regular beating is to crack, shortly, returning to kill

indicators.note: shortly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: to crack is to snap

indicators.note: returning means the word for kill is read backwards

parts.note: to kill is to murder

explanation.surface: A victim of repeated beatings is about to snap and kill in return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' cuts SNAP to SNA; 'returning' turns MURDER into REDRUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A drummer strikes this small military drum in steady rhythm, so it receives regular beats.

clue.text: Australia is on standby, protecting intermediaries

indicators.note: protecting means the words hold the answer inside them

explanation.surface: Australia's forces on alert to defend someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Liaison officers act as go-betweens linking two parties, so they are intermediaries.

clue.text: Heathen to search for gold (silver is boring)

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so silver goes inside

parts.note: prospectors pan for gold by washing gravel in a dish
AG is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: An unbeliever off prospecting for gold, finding silver dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' looks like 'dull' in the bracket but means drilling into.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of a non-mainstream or pre-Christian religion was called a heathen.

clue.text: Paces about, tense in appearance

indicators.note: about means the letters are turned around and rearranged

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Someone pacing nervously, looking tense.
explanation.definitionFit: The look or outward side of something, as a building's aspect, is its appearance.

clue.text: Occasionally, treat an American for disease

indicators.note: occasionally means only every other letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: Giving an American a treat now and then in place of an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Lockjaw, the bacterial infection causing muscle spasms, is a serious illness.
